name: Notion
summary: Public connections work for any workspace without review; only a Marketplace listing is reviewed, and the installation scope can never be changed.

capabilities.label: Search and read pages and databases the user shares
capabilities.alternative: Users choose specific pages in the page picker during consent

capabilities.label: Create and update pages, blocks and database entries

paths.label: Public connection limited to selected workspaces
paths.drivenBy: Create a public connection with installation scope 'Selected workspaces only', set redirect URI and capabilities, copy client ID and secret into Composio. Scope cannot be changed later, and this connection can never be listed.
paths.next: Create a public connection in the Notion Developer portal with 'Selected workspaces only' and register https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add as the redirect URI.

untilApproved.text: Only workspaces chosen at creation can install the connection.

paths.label: Public connection for any workspace, unlisted
paths.drivenBy: Create a public connection with installation scope 'Any workspace'. Notion says it can be used through its OAuth flow without being listed. Each user authorizes individually and picks pages. Keep the client secret in a secret manager.
paths.next: Create a public connection with installation scope 'Any workspace' so it stays eligible for a later Marketplace listing.

untilApproved.text: No review needed; any Notion user can install via OAuth without a listing.
Each workspace member must authorize separately; access is per user.

paths.label: Optional Notion Marketplace listing
paths.drivenBy: Listing is optional; listed connections pass a Notion security review first, then listing review.
paths.next: Draft a listing under Listings > Connections in the Marketplace listing dashboard and submit for review.

untilApproved.text: The connection still works through OAuth for any workspace while the listing is pending.
If changes are required, Notion emails feedback and you can resubmit.

prereqs.text: Decide the installation scope before creating the connection: 'Selected workspaces only' for your own workspaces, 'Any workspace' for customers or a Marketplace listing.
prereqs.why: Installation scope is set at creation and cannot be changed. Listing a 'Selected workspaces only' connection later means creating a new connection.

prereqs.text: Have a Notion account with access to the Developer portal and a workspace to use as the development workspace.
prereqs.why: Development workspace is a required field when creating a public connection.

prereqs.text: Set up a secret manager for the OAuth client secret.
prereqs.why: Notion says never to expose a client secret in page source and to use a secret manager for deployed apps.

prereqs.text: Prepare listing assets: name, description, category, tags, images and logo.
prereqs.why: These are the required fields for a Marketplace listing draft.

steps.title: Choose the installation scope
steps.detail: Pick 'Selected workspaces only' for team-only use and list the workspaces now. Pick 'Any workspace' for customers or if you may list on the Marketplace later. This cannot be changed after creation.

steps.title: Create a public connection in the Notion Developer portal
steps.detail: Create a public (OAuth) connection. Enter the connection name, development workspace, redirect URI, installation scope and capabilities. Select only the capabilities your agent needs. Select only the content, comment and user-information capabilities your agent needs. Do not use an internal connection or a personal access token, because those are not for other users' accounts.

values.label: Capabilities to cover
values.text: read content; write content (create/update pages, blocks, database entries); comments (read and add); user information

steps.title: Copy the client ID, client secret and authorization URL
steps.detail: Open the Configuration tab of the connection. Copy the OAuth client ID, the client secret and the authorization URL. Store the secret in your secret manager.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config with your own credentials
steps.detail: Create a Composio auth config for the notion toolkit that uses your client ID and client secret instead of the Composio managed app. Confirm that the redirect URI registered in Notion matches exactly.

steps.title: Test the OAuth flow with a test workspace
steps.detail: Start a connection through the new auth config. Check that Notion shows your connection's capability prompt and the page picker. Share test pages, then confirm the agent can read and write only those pages. For 'Selected workspaces only', use one of the workspaces you chose.

steps.title: Switch agent connections to the new auth config
steps.detail: Point new Notion connections at your auth config. Existing users connected through the Composio managed app must reconnect. Each user gets their own token, and other members of the same workspace must authorize separately.

steps.title: Draft the Marketplace listing
steps.detail: In the Marketplace listing dashboard (Listings > Connections), start a draft. Fill in the name, description, category, tags, images, logo and the associated public connection. The connection must use the 'Any workspace' scope. Avoid brand or trademark conflicts.

steps.title: Submit the listing for review
steps.detail: Submit the draft. Listing is optional, and the connection already works through OAuth without it.

steps.title: Wait for Notion's listing review
steps.detail: Notion reviews every listing submission and replies by email. This is Notion's stated timeline. No measured timelines from developers were found.

steps.title: Apply feedback and resubmit if changes are requested
steps.detail: If Notion requests changes, update the listing and resubmit.

steps.title: Roll out the connect flow to users
steps.detail: Send users through the Composio connect link. Each user authorizes individually and picks the pages the agent can access. Tell users that pages they do not pick are not visible to the agent.

gotchas.text: Installation scope is permanent. A 'Selected workspaces only' connection can never be listed, and only the workspaces chosen at creation can install it.
No review is needed for external users to connect. Listing is optional, and an unlisted 'Any workspace' connection works through its OAuth flow.
Access is per user. Other members of the same workspace must each authorize, and the agent sees only the pages chosen in the page picker.
The authorize URL begins with https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize; the token exchange uses HTTP Basic with your client ID and secret.
Each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token. Store both.
Rate limits: 600 requests a minute per connection on Business and Enterprise, 180 on other plans, plus a per-workspace limit shared by all connections.
Notion's MCP server registers clients itself (dynamic registration and client ID metadata documents), but an MCP token works only with Notion MCP, not the REST API that Composio's toolkit uses.
Enterprise workspaces can be set to approved connections only.
Authorization codes are reported to expire within seconds, so exchange them immediately (forum report).

blockers.cause: The redirect URI sent in the request differs from the one registered on the connection.
blockers.fix: Register exactly https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add on the connection and use the same value in the Composio auth config.

blockers.cause: The code or refresh token is invalid, expired or revoked, or does not match the redirect URI used in the authorization request.
blockers.fix: Restart the authorization, exchange the code immediately, and check that the redirect URI and client secret match.

blockers.cause: The client ID or secret is wrong or unknown, or the Authorization header is malformed.
blockers.fix: Re-copy the client ID and secret from the Configuration tab into the auth config. Send them as Basic auth, as Notion's docs show.

blockers.see: Invalid redirect_uri for OAuth client with Notion's hosted MCP server
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri, a random localhost port, is not in the client metadata allowlist.
blockers.fix: Use a fixed redirect URI that is listed in the client's allowed redirects. This applies to the hosted MCP flow, not to your own connection.

blockers.cause: The connection uses 'Selected workspaces only' scope, or it is an internal connection.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with 'Any workspace' scope and attach it to the listing.

blockers.see: Listing rejected or changes requested by email
blockers.cause: Brand or trademark issues, quality concerns, or not meeting the baseline connection criteria.
blockers.fix: Address the emailed reason, check the Connection Gallery Best Practices guide, update the listing and resubmit.

aiPolicy.summary: Notion's Developer Terms (2 Apr 2026) have no AI-specific clause, but data read through the API may be used only to provide your connection's features, for no other purpose, and never without the user's consent. Read literally, that rules out training models on workspace content.

customerAdminNote: Notion Enterprise owners can limit members to approved connections only. Ask their workspace owner to approve your connection before rollout.
